statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail eases to 15 as the opening auction and the first cash hour resolve with observed two-way structure. NQ at 30,206.00 on the 10:16 ET delayed quote sits about 45 points above a 30,161.00 post-open low and about 137 points below the 30,343.00 session high, so a fresh low was made and recovered rather than extended. NAHB printed a benign 35. Tail remains well below the block threshold.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with a mean-reverting regime carrying a narrow, semiconductor-led upward tilt. The single most important input this hour is that NQ made a new session low at 30,161.00 into the cash open and bought it back to 30,206.00, leaving the contract mid-range rather than holding near an extreme. The 14:00Z NAHB release printed 35 against a consensus near 33 and did not break the range. Cross-asset evidence stays two-sided, with technology the only advancing S&P 500 sector, megacaps six down and two up, the 2-year lower and the 10-year higher on the day, WTI flat at $82.45 and the VIX contained in a 14.89-15.09 band. Tail eases to 15, Stress eases to 64 and Confidence rises to 85. The mapped policy state is EA_ON. The danger window is narrowed to the 19:00Z-20:00Z power hour, the remaining interval in which a directionally efficient close with shallow pullbacks would most plausibly develop.
headline: NQ near 30,206 holds mid-range after making and recovering a 30,161 post-open low, with NAHB at 35, the VIX at 15.03, the 10-year near 4.70% and Brent near $88.84
body:
NQ futures were 30,206.00 on a 10:16 ET delayed quote, up about 64.25 points or 0.21% on the 30,141.75 prior settlement, inside an observed session band of roughly 30,161.00-30,343.00. The structurally decisive fact of this hour is that the opening auction and the first cash hour produced a new session low at 30,161.00, roughly 21 points below the pre-open low, and then recovered it. The contract now sits about 45 points above that low and about 137 points below the 30,343.00 high set after the 12:30Z Empire State release. NQ is mid-range on both sides.

That is direct evidence against the pathological price path this assessment is designed to detect. A no-retracement regime does not make a fresh low into the cash open and then buy it back; it extends. The prior hour could only record that a retracement from the session high had occurred with the opening auction still ahead. This hour has the opening auction behind it and the retracement holding, which is why tail risk eases from 16 to 15 rather than simply repeating.

The 14:00Z NAHB Housing Market Index printed 35 against a consensus near 33 and 34 prior, with current sales conditions at 39, six-month expectations at 43 and prospective buyer traffic at 23. A one-point improvement from a depressed base is a benign outcome and did not produce a directional break in either direction.

Cross-asset evidence remains two-sided, which under this framework raises Stress rather than tail risk. The cash tape is split: the S&P 500 near 7,773 and the Dow near 53,559 are both modestly lower while the Nasdaq holds a small gain, and technology is the only S&P 500 sector advancing. Megacaps are six down and two up on the latest session, with Microsoft near -2.2% and Meta near -1.7% against Nvidia and Broadcom marginally higher. Semiconductors are the exception and the session's momentum axis, with Micron crossing $1,000 per share after a 36% rally from its late-July lows on hyperscaler memory demand, alongside reporting that Anthropic's quarterly revenue rose to more than $11.5 billion. Leadership that narrow supports an index without producing broad one-way structure.

The macro backdrop keeps Stress elevated at 64. The 10-year sits near 4.70% and the 30-year at 5.28%, close to 19-month highs, gold is extending toward roughly $4,442 on debt concerns, and Brent near $88.84 reflects Strait of Hormuz transit disruption and stalled US-Iran talks rather than an actual supply outage. None of these is currently aligned with equity direction: the 2-year is a touch lower on the day while the 10-year is a touch higher, and WTI is effectively flat at $82.45. The VIX at 15.03 is up 5.5% on the day but confined to a 14.89-15.09 range, which is volatility repricing without volatility expansion.

Confidence rises to 85. The post-open price path is now observed rather than inferred, the NAHB actual has been verified against the primary release, and delayed cross-asset context collected at 14:13Z corroborates the live reads on futures direction, rates and energy.

The published danger window is narrowed to the 19:00Z-20:00Z power hour. The opening-auction interval flagged an hour ago has now resolved without pathological structure, and the remaining interval in which a directionally efficient close with shallow pullbacks could plausibly develop is the last cash hour, which also carries the 20:00Z TIC Flows release.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Tail stayed inside the low band for the entire window, ranging from 12 to 17, with the mapped policy state EA_ON throughout. Stress peaked at 82 during Sunday's US-hours window while Gulf conflict and crude headlines dominated, then decayed steadily to 65 in the final hour as the tape compressed. Confidence improved from 78 to 84, with a temporary dip to 68 across the thin Sunday evening hours, as live futures pricing, volatility, rates and calendar evidence became progressively better corroborated. Dominant mode was mixed through the active sessions and normal across the quiet overnight stretch. At no point in the window was a persistent no-retracement path observed. The final three hours captured the hot Empire State print, the orderly two-way repricing that followed it, and the cash open itself.
outlookSummary: The conditional path keeps tail risk inside the low band across all 24 forecast hours, with the mapped policy state EA_ON throughout. Conditional risk sits at 15 in the current hour, lifts to 16 across the 15:00Z hour where opening imbalances clear and pullback depth becomes readable, then eases through the US afternoon to 14. It returns to 16 in the 19:00Z power hour, the published danger window and the interval most capable of producing a directionally efficient close, before falling to a window minimum of 12 across the thin post-close and Asian hours. It rebuilds gradually through the Tuesday European session to 14 and peaks at 17 in the 12:00Z and 13:00Z slots, which contain the 12:30Z Housing Starts and Building Permits release and the 13:15Z Industrial Production release ahead of the Tuesday cash open. Stress eases from 64 to a low of 55 overnight before rebuilding to 65 into the Tuesday data block. Confidence decays from 85 to about 76 across the hours where no live price path is observable and recovers to 79 as the new European session forms.

forecastDetail.comment: NQ at 30,206 sits mid-range, roughly 45 points above the 30,161 post-open low and 137 below the 30,343 session high; the opening auction produced a new low that was recovered rather than extended, and NAHB printed 35 against 33 expected.

Opening imbalances normally clear in this hour, making the depth of the next pullback the cleaner read on mean reversion; conditional risk lifts one point for that missing read, not for observed one-way structure.

Midday liquidity decay usually suppresses range expansion, and two full cash hours would by now have exposed repeated extension after failed retracements if it were present, so conditional risk eases.

European close has passed and the US afternoon lull typically dominates; conditional risk reaches its US-session low while long-end yields and gold stay a standing Stress input rather than a price-path amplifier.
A quiet positioning hour ahead of the last cash hour; the useful checkpoint is whether the day has built a clear directional imbalance into the close.

Power hour and the published danger window: late-session flow is where a directionally efficient close with shallow pullbacks would most plausibly appear, so conditional risk peaks for the US session, with TIC Flows at 20:00Z.
